Three one-time steps. Completed steps are detected automatically when you come back here.
Flip2 Layout Switcher uses Shizuku, a free open-source app, to change the controller setting without root. Install it from Google Play, then come back here.

Start Shizuku with Wireless debugging (no computer needed). Shizuku’s own guide walks you through it:
1. Connect to Wi-Fi. Turn on Developer options: Settings → About handheld console → tap Build number 7 times.
2. In Shizuku tap Pairing and allow its notifications when asked.
3. In Settings → System → Developer options → Wireless debugging, choose Pair device with pairing code and type the code into Shizuku’s notification.
4. Back in Shizuku tap Start, then return here.
Shizuku is running. Allow Flip2 Layout Switcher to use it.
Open Accessibility settings, tap Flip2 Layout Switcher under Downloaded apps and turn on Use Flip2 Layout Switcher. Only app names are detected; screen text and key presses are not read.
Permission blocked or app not listed?

If Android blocks the accessibility permission, open App info, use the three-dot menu and select Allow restricted settings. Then return to Accessibility settings and enable Flip2 Layout Switcher. You approve this permission yourself.
After restarting your device, open Shizuku and tap Start again (Wi-Fi needed). Your profiles and the other steps are kept.

On Retroid, clearing Recents force-stops apps, which turns automatic switching off. In Handheld Settings open Advanced → Whitelist application → menu (⋮) → Add whitelist, tick Flip2 Layout Switcher and tap the save icon, then come back here.
Power → Clean process when standby is on and will stop Flip2 Layout Switcher when the screen turns off. Turn it off, or add Flip2 Layout Switcher to the apps it ignores.
Flip2 Layout Switcher is whitelisted; clearing Recents will not stop it.
On by default: when the app opens, look for a newer release on GitHub (at most every 6 hours).
A newer version of Flip2 Layout Switcher is available.
Open-source controller profiles for Retroid Pocket Flip 2. Uses the existing Retroid controller setting. No virtual controller, ads or data collection.

Installed app names and profiles stay on this device. App detection uses window package metadata only. No screen content or key logging. The only network access is the update check against this project’s GitHub Releases; it is on by default and can be turned off in Settings. Diagnostics contain recent package names and are kept in app-private storage.
Test A / B / X / Y buttons
Press a physical A, B, X or Y button. Testing stops 10 seconds after the last press.
